Uses of Package
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.login

Packages that use com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.login
Package
Description
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web
Web adapter of the authorization server: security filter chains, login page and OpenAPI description.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.error
Error page of the server-rendered pages.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.implicit
OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628) for input-constrained clients, such as a command line tool: the protocol customizer that wires the device authorization and verification endpoints, the guard that applies the multi-factor policy and the limit on the attempts to the verification endpoint, and the verification page.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.login
Login page, its controller and the extension points other authentication methods plug into.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.logout
 
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa
Multi-factor authentication orchestration.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ott
One-time token authentication: e-mail and SMS codes and magic links as a primary sign-in method and as a second factor, the per-channel factors, the rate limits, the providers and filters, and the phone management API and account page.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.pages
Rendering of the server-rendered HTML pages.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.passkeys
Passkeys (WebAuthn): the factor, the chain wiring, the login and second-factor fragments, the account API and the account page.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.password
Web adapter of the password-based sign-in: the Spring Security user details service over the use case, the password encoder and the authentication provider, which checks the account status only after the password.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.social
Social login (identity brokering) through external identity providers: Google, Microsoft Entra ID, Apple and GitHub.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.totp
Time-based one-time password (TOTP) second factor.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509
X.509 client certificate authentication: a certificate presented on a dedicated TLS port, or forwarded by a trusted reverse proxy in a header, signs in the user it is bound to (by the SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate) at POST /login/x509, the form of the login page, with the CSRF token.

  • Classes in com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.login used by com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.login
    Class
    Description
    BrandingProperties
    Branding shown by the login, consent, logout and error pages, bound from authserver.ui.branding.*.
    LoginChainCustomizer
    Extension point that lets an authentication method customize the login/UI security filter chain.
    LoginContentSecurityPolicy
    Builds the content security policy of the server-rendered pages from the BrandingProperties: same-origin resources only and no framing, except that images may also be data: URIs (the QR code of an authenticator app, rendered in memory so its secret never becomes a resource of its own) and, when the branding logo is an absolute http(s) URL, come from its origin (img-src 'self' data: <scheme://host[:port]>).
    LoginErrorMessages
    Maps the exception of a failed sign-in, which Spring Security keeps in the SPRING_SECURITY_LAST_EXCEPTION session attribute, to the key of the message the login page shows.
    LoginMethodFragment
    Extension point that lets an authentication method contribute a Thymeleaf fragment to the login page.
